business_problem: The Royal Melbourne Hospital needed to replace fragmented pager, phone, ticketing, and paper workflows used by facilities teams because those siloed processes made it hard to manage service requests, track assets, support compliance, and respond quickly during growing operational demand.
solution_summary: Royal Melbourne Hospital implemented IBM TRIRIGA as an integrated workplace management system and mobile task-management platform for facilities operations. The hospital first reviewed business processes, then used a CAFM project team to digitize facilities workflows spanning cleaning, maintenance, engineering, patient transport, pathology delivery, and many other non-clinical services across multiple campuses and satellite locations. TRIRIGA Request Central lets clinical and facilities teams submit and monitor work from smart devices, while dashboards surface real-time job status, outstanding work, asset details, and service trends. IBM Cloud Delivery Services runs the solution as a managed service from an IBM data center, and the platform continues to expand into asset management, energy management, space management, and planned IoT integrations. Because the system replaced several disconnected tools with a unified workflow and analytics layer, RMH gained the operational resilience needed to accelerate its COVID-era go-live and to support clinical throughput with more transparent, data-driven service operations.

data_flow: Service requests from wards, emergency, allied health, and other stakeholders flow into TRIRIGA Request Central, tasks are assigned to facilities teams through mobile devices and dashboards, and resulting activity, asset, and response data feeds hospital reporting and future planning modules.
business_outcome: RMH digitized facilities operations at scale, improved service-response times, reduced paper use and waste, supported COVID-era cleaning and tracing needs, and created a platform for broader asset, space, energy, and IoT-driven operational improvement.
